claims.statement: TaskForge is at least once; current delivery identity and owner fence ack, retry, dead-letter, and lease extension.
Retry is bounded and identity-preserving, and DLQ publication precedes source acknowledgement.
Delayed and recurring scheduler writes require the current leadership fence.
New publishes choose routing while retry, release, recurrence, DLQ, and recovery preserve placement.
Environment decoding and embedded applications use the canonical taskforge.Config model without a sidecar-owned runtime copy.
Sensitive HTTP routes require authentication or are absent, responses redact task payload/results, and bounded server limits default on.
Validated startup accepts only a writable direct standalone Redis primary and makes TLS configuration explicit.
Named deterministic simulation seeds and bounded exhaustive models exercise documented ownership and fencing mutations.
The release dry-run verifies supported binary and image evidence without publishing.
The public demo and comparative smoke workloads are executable contracts; benchmark output is not an SLA or superiority claim.

assumptions.statement: Applications make external handler side effects idempotent; TaskForge does not provide exactly-once effects.
Operators configure Redis persistence, replication, backup, recovery, and capacity for their durability needs.
Operators use a trusted TLS reverse proxy and authentication for non-loopback HTTP exposure and protect Redis credentials and CA material.
Liveness assumes bounded pauses, a sufficiently accurate local clock, and eventual access to a writable Redis primary.
Race, simulation, model, benchmark, and vulnerability checks are bounded evidence rather than proof of defect absence or performance superiority.
